To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Gd‐EOD‐enhanced MRI is useful for differentiating between hepatocellular nodular lesions during hepatocarcininogenesis, and that the expression of the Gd‐EOBDTPA transporter OATP1B3 is correlated with the enhancement pattern.

the signal intensity on Gd‐EOO‐DTPA‐enhanced MRI of various hepatocellular lesions during hepatocarcino‐genesis is associated with the expression of the transporters, and that Gd‐EOOB‐DTPA may be useful for differentiating hepatocellular nodular lesions.
the signal enhancement ratio (SER) of Gd‐EB‐DTPA‐enhanced MRI is higher for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), lower for dysplastic nodules (DNs), and lowest for non‐cancerous nodules.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of the transporter of Gd‐EB‐DTPA was decreased in hepatocarcinogenic nodules and that Gd‐EBD‐DTPA‐enhanced MRI could be used to differentiate hepatocellular nodular lesions in hepatocarcino‐genesis.

the expression of the transporters for Gd‐EOE‐DTPA is altered during hepatocarcarcinogenesis, and that the change in the expression of these transporters is related to the change in the signal intensity on Gd‐EOEB‐DTPA‐enhanced MRI.
